title: Tenant key topologies and quota playbook demo - Verde Pipelines
summary: AE+SE walkthrough of org/project key topologies, quota patterns, and tenant isolation strategies for a data-processing SaaS. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private, RBAC/SSO/KMS concerns, pricing implications of burst policies, and next steps to run a benchmark pilot and share security docs.
action_items: Maya Patel: Send pilot proposal and pricing spreadsheet (due 2026-11-09)
Connor Li: Share sample benchmark script and test API keys (due 2026-11-06)
Aisha Khan: Provide representative traffic patterns and top 50 orgs by qps (due 2026-11-10)
next_steps: Redwood to run 48h benchmark on Verde dev dataset with dedicated pool config
Customer to review security docs (SOC2 report, SAML SSO guide, KMS integration notes)
Schedule follow-up deep dive with infra team next week (30-45min)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-04 10:00am PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Aisha (Verde CTO), Tom (Lead SRE), Lena (Product)

Summary auto-gen: Walkthrough of keying strategies for multi-tenant quota control; demo of console patterns and API behaviors.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya, i'm the AE on this account, quick round robin?
00:18 Aisha: hi i'm aisha, CTO at Verde Pipelines, thanks for doing this, we've been looking at rate limits and how to do quotas across our customers, basically trying to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
00:36 Tom: tom here, lead SRE, we run around lots of small tenants and a few big ones, so capacity planning is a headache.
00:45 Maya: perfect, today connor will walk through the org/project key topologies and some playbook patterns. we've shared a short deck -- link in chat -- and a spreadsheet with sample qps distributions.
01:05 Connor: cool, i'll start with a quick map of patterns. there are two axes we usually talk about: identity mapping (org vs project keys) and quota slicing (hard v soft, concurrency v token). so first pattern is single-org-key with projects pinned via subkeys, second is per-project keys with org aggregation, third is mixed hybrid with sticky routing.
01:40 Lena: can you explain sticky routing again? we've seen that term but unclear on stickiness guarantees.
01:49 Connor: sure. sticky routing means requests from a given api key are preferentially routed to the same serving pool to preserve cache/KV locality. that reduces cold kv misses and gives more predictable latencies. it's not absolute; we have fallback lanes in case capacity shifts.
02:15 Tom: how often does sticky routing cause imbalance? if a big customer gets sticky lane and then spikes, does it starve others?
02:25 Connor: good question. we use fairburst policies plus leak-y bucket smoothing, so by default we allow short spikes but after X seconds the router will re-balance or redirect to overflow capacity. you can tune thresholds per org or project.
02:45 Aisha: i want the pattern that limits blast radius but doesn't create too many keys for our customer UI. we have a lot of internal teams who create projects.
02:56 Connor: that's where org-project hierarchy helps. use org key for admin operations and per-project keys for production workloads. also set project-level concurrency quotas and org-level cumulative quotas.
03:15 Maya: note that the console lets you create quota templates so you can apply consistent policies across new projects.
03:27 Aisha: okay show us the console.
03:30 Connor: switching to demo. (screen) this is the policies page. you can see a template called "small-tenant-default" and one called "enterprise-committed". templates control concurrency, token rate, burst allowances and backpressure thresholds.
04:00 Connor: i'll click into "enterprise-committed" -- it has a guaranteed throughput lane with reserved capacity and a lower-cost best-effort lane. customers on dedicated capacity typically use reserved lanes for latency-sensitive endpoints.
04:30 Tom: reserved capacity = Dedicated product?
04:33 Connor: yes. Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool with predictable throughput and no noisy neighbor from host. hosted customers can still get similar behavior with committed tiers but if you need full isolation, Private with VPC is our on-prem/VPC option.
04:53 Aisha: we are evaluating private for certain regulated pipelines, what's the lift for KMS/HSM?
04:59 Connor: Private supports customer-managed KMS, you can bring your own HSM in on-prem cases. for VPC we integrate with cloud KMS and support rotation policies and audit logs.
05:18 Lena: can we get SSO mapped to RBAC so product teams only spin up dev keys but not billing keys?
05:26 Connor: yep, SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning works, and RBAC policies let you limit who can create org-level keys. you can also enable key-scoped roles. we'll share the SSO guide.
05:45 Maya: quick plug about audit logs — we store token-level traces and per-request metadata in the console for X days depending on retention tier, and you can forward logs to your SIEM.
06:05 Aisha: SOC2? we need to know if you have SOC2 & ISO certs for procurement.
06:12 Maya: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001, i'll attach the reports.
06:18 Aisha: perfect.
06:23 Connor: back to quota topologies: here's a scenario we modelled for a mixed tenant distribution. (screen shows chart) top 10 tenants produce 70% of qps, the remainder is long tail. For long tail we usually apply per-project low concurrency and a higher token rate but with tight bursts. For the top tenants we give dedicated lanes or a higher org cumulative quota.
06:54 Tom: does the router support per-org fallback to a cheaper quantized model if the fast model is busy?
07:02 Connor: yes, you can configure model variant fallbacks. we often use quantized variants for cost-savings; they're pinned in catalog as compatible fallbacks.
07:18 Lena: implication for cost: if a top tenant is bursty and we route them to dedicated, that ups our committed spend. how is that billed?
07:27 Maya: billing for Dedicated is reserved monthly capacity plus overage for burst. For hosted, it's usage-based per token plus optional overcommit burst fees. we'll include a sample pricing scenario in the spreadsheet.
07:46 Aisha: can we set a hard deny on certain routes? e.g., block a tenant from generating embeddings if they hit quota?
07:55 Connor: yes, policies support deny actions, rate-limited actions, and backpressure that returns 429 or queues requests. you can also route to a cheaper model or return graceful degradation responses via webhook.
08:20 Maya: question from procurement side often: can you support per-tenant billing keys?
08:27 Connor: you can mint project-level keys and attach billing metadata so events attribute to tenant. many customers forward usage to their billing system using per-project keys.
08:40 Tom: about concurrency limits — do you expose ephemeral token concurrency or is it per api-key?
08:46 Connor: we track both. concurrency is measured per API key by default but you can set namespace-level or org-level concurrency windows. there's also namespace sticky counter if you map projects to namespaces.
09:05 Aisha: we want a playbook recommendation for onboarding 1k+ tenants gradually.
09:13 Connor: recommended: start with org default template, auto-provision project keys on sign-up with low defaults, enable auto-escalation rules for projects that pass threshold X, and schedule a canary capacity bump for big tenants. we also recommend a sandbox pool for staging.
09:34 Lena: can those auto-escalation rules be manual review? we have compliance constraints.
09:40 Connor: yes, auto-escalation can require approval. workflows integrate with your ticketing system via webhooks.
09:50 Maya: quick check: are there any compliance controls we should call out?
09:54 Connor: audit logs, KMS, SAML, VPC, optional air-gapped private deployment for regulated workloads. we also support egress filtering on Private.
10:10 Aisha: we heard from another vendor about token-based throttles that cause partial completions — is that a problem here?
10:18 Connor: you can choose to throttle at request boundary or token boundary. we recommend request boundary for deterministic behavior, token boundary for strict token budgets but it can lead to truncated outputs.
10:34 Tom: perf question — what latency can we expect for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on hosted vs dedicated?
10:42 Connor: median p50 for short prompts on hosted is usually 50-80ms for optimized models, dedicated p50 closer to 30-45ms depending on GPU type. for quantized variants add ~10-20ms. these are ballpark; we'll run benchmarks with your prompts.
11:05 Lena: that sounds good. can you demo the API behavior for quota exceeded?
11:12 Connor: sure. (switch) I'll make a test call with a low concurrency quota and show the 429 and headers like x-rate-limit-remaining and x-retry-after.
11:35 Connor: ok sent a burst, see 429 with retry-after 13s, response body includes a short explanation. sometimes the transcript shows header keys as x-rw-... but in our doc they're listed. apologies for any typos.
11:53 Aisha: nice to see the headers. do you include request ids for tracing?
11:58 Connor: yep, every request has a request_id and span id for tracing, and the console lets you click into the trace.
12:10 Maya: procurement also asks about long term retention for logs, can we keep 12 months?
12:16 Connor: retention tiers are configurable; long-term retention is a paid add-on and you can export logs to your S3 or SIEM.
12:30 Tom: what about egress data residency? some customers in EU want EU-only inference.
12:36 Maya: we have regionalized hosting and Private VPC on-prem. you can pin routes to region and configure failover.
12:46 Aisha: okay, show an example of a per-project quota template being applied and an override at org-level.
12:52 Connor: (demo) creating a project template: set concurrency 5, token rate 2000/min, burst 50 tokens. then i apply to project, and at the org-level i set a cumulative concurrency of 200 so org sum can't exceed that. override is supported and we show precedence in UI.
13:26 Lena: do you support quotas by route? we have some endpoints that are embedding heavy and others generation heavy.
13:33 Connor: yes, you can scope quotas to model family or route tag, so embeddings can be isolated. routing policies let you route embedding requests to optimized pools with separate quotas.
13:48 Tom: what's the default behavior when a quota template is updated—do existing projects inherit or stay pinned?
13:55 Connor: updates to templates do not retroactively change pinned projects unless you choose "apply to existing" checkbox. it's explicit to prevent surprise changes.
14:10 Aisha: we also want to control noise from our non-prod environments, can you rate-limit by key age or label?
14:18 Connor: yes, labels and metadata on keys can be used in policy expressions. common pattern: label env=staging and impose lower quotas.
14:30 Maya: a short aside about Optimize — our suggestions engine analyzes your traffic and suggests batching and quantization levels. it can recommend lowering token precision for embedding-only workloads. sometimes the auto-suggest called "Redwood Optima" in older docs — apologies that's misspoken — it's Redwood Optimize.
14:56 Lena: does Optimize do automatic rollouts? could it flip a model variant in prod?
15:03 Connor: Optimize provides recommendations and an optional automated rollout pipeline under strict guardrails. most customers prefer manual approval for production.
15:18 Tom: on the pilot: we want to test 48h of traffic with our histogram patterns and see cost delta between hosted and dedicated. what's minimal setup?
15:27 Connor: minimal pilot: a dedicated test pool sized to match your p95 and a host fallback lane. we'll provide test API keys and a script that simulates your traffic profile. expected setup time ~1-2 days.
15:39 Aisha: data concerns — will any customer data leave our VPC during the pilot?
15:45 Connor: for hosted pilot, requests traverse Redwood hosted infra; logs can be configured to exclude raw payloads, but for strict data residency you should use Private. for initial benchmarking many customers are comfortable sending pseudo or anonymized data.
16:04 Lena: okay please include the anonymization checklist.
16:09 Maya: noted. we'll include checklist and a small runbook.
16:14 Connor: there's also a pattern we recommend for onboarding: sandbox pool -> stage pool with same quotas but smaller tokens -> prod with graduated quotas and reserved lanes for big tenants.
16:33 Tom: any gotchas around API key rotation and long-running streams? we use streaming responses for logs.
16:40 Connor: streaming is supported; for rotation we recommend short-lived project tokens for ephemeral tasks and longer-lived org tokens for admin. you can revoke keys and the router will gracefully drain KV caches associated with that key.
16:58 Aisha: good. procurement will want a sample contract clause about data segregation.
17:04 Maya: we'll pass a standard clause and can work with legal.
17:09 Lena: do you have examples of observability dashboards for per-tenant cost?
17:15 Connor: yes, console has token-level cost breakdown at token and route level. you can export per-project cost to CSV or to your billing pipeline via webhook.
17:28 Tom: competitor comp check: OtherCloudAI tried to sell us with unlimited burst but poor latency under load. how are your backpressure guarantees different?
17:36 Connor: our backpressure aims for graceful degradation: route to fallback model, return informative 429s, or queue at the edge with a configured max wait. unlimited burst is risky for noisy neighbors.
17:50 Aisha: ok what's the next step?
17:52 Maya: recap: we'll send pilot proposal and pricing, connor sends benchmark artifacts, verde provides traffic pattern and signs NDA for pilot data if needed. schedule follow-up deep-dive next week.
18:05 Lena: thanks all.
18:10 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
